what_happened: Job 20261030-125332-sz3z ("Count only 'Depends on' ids and retry links as plan dependencies") ended failed before its checks ran. The free-disk guard found 10.0 GB free and 10.0 GB required, so it stopped the job with an environment message. The message says the cause is the environment, not the work. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet, no findings were raised and no checks ran. The work was not judged and nothing was delivered. Someone has to free disk and run `athena retry`.
cause: Athena treats free disk as a precondition it only tests right before the checks. It neither reclaims space it owns (old build targets, finished job working copies) nor checks space at admission or before dispatch. The producer therefore spends its budget and then the job ends failed on an environment limit. The job also fails in a state that offers only a manual retry. The dependency fix it carries is the one that stops evidence-citing requests being held, so the stop delays work that other queued items need.
prevention: Before dispatching a job, Athena would check free disk against the same threshold the pre-check guard uses, and would reclaim space it owns first: finished jobs' build directories and stale working copies. If space is still short, it would hold the job as waiting on the environment instead of failing it. The producer's work would be kept, and the job would resume on its own once space returns, with no the person running Athena step and no counted failure.
proposed_request: Make Athena handle low free disk without failing jobs. (1) Before dispatching a job and again before its checks, compare free disk to the required amount. (2) If it is short, automatically delete only space Athena owns: build targets and working copies of jobs that are landed, closed or failed. Then re-measure. (3) If space is still short, put the job on hold with a clear 'waiting for disk' status, keep the producer's work, and do not count it as a failure or as line spend. (4) Resume the held job automatically once the free space reaches the requirement. Acceptance: a test with a fake disk measure shows a job at exactly the threshold is cleaned and then runs to its checks. A test shows a job that cannot be freed is held, not failed, and resumes when space is added. A test shows cleanup never touches a running job's directories.
